questions.question: Sandra Cisneros's 1984 novella The House on Mango Street made a lasting impact on US literature. Its depiction of Mexican American culture inspired later authors to examine their own heritage within their fictional works. Also influential was the book's portrayal of the main character, Esperanza, during a pivotal year of her youth. This insightful depiction of a preteen girl encouraged authors who, like Cisneros herself, are Latina to use fictional works to examine experiences from their own youth. Which statement, if true, would most strongly support the claim in the underlined sentence?
options: In interviews, a number of Latina authors say that The House on Mango Street inspired them to write about their own adolescence in their novels.
In published writings, several prominent authors who are not Latina say that reading The House on Mango Street influenced their approach to writing fiction.
The House on Mango Street has sold over six million copies and is one of the most commonly read books among high school and university students in the US.
Since 1984, new novels about young Latina characters by Latina authors have often been compared to The House on Mango Street.

questions.question:
Botanist Rui Alvarez compared seed germination under three conditions: bare soil, a thin layer of fallen leaves, and a thick layer of fallen leaves. Germination was highest under the thin layer and lowest under the thick layer. These results support Alvarez's claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: seeds germinate only when no leaves cover the soil.
any amount of leaf litter prevents seeds from receiving water.
thick leaf litter always increases the amount of light reaching seeds.
a modest amount of leaf litter can aid germination, but too much can hinder it.
questions.explanation: D is correct because it accounts for both findings: the thin layer outperformed bare soil, whereas the thick layer performed worst.

questions.question:
Historian Mina Okafor compared nineteenth-century ship captains' logs with repair records from the ports those ships visited. The logs mentioned fewer repairs than the port records did, and the difference was largest after periods of rough weather. Okafor argues that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

captains accurately recorded every repair made during rough weather.
ships required fewer repairs after periods of rough weather.
repair records are useful only when captains' logs are unavailable.
questions.explanation: A is correct because the port records consistently contain repair evidence absent from the logs, especially after rough weather.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Two groups of music students practiced the same four short passages. One group practiced each passage repeatedly before moving to the next; the other alternated among the passages. On a later test using a new passage, the alternating group adjusted to changes in rhythm more successfully. The result supports the conclusion that ______

alternating among tasks can improve the transfer of a skill to unfamiliar material.
students learn rhythm only when they practice a single passage.
the new passage was identical to the four practice passages.
questions.explanation: B is correct because the alternating group's stronger performance on unfamiliar material is evidence of skill transfer.

questions.question:
Researchers observed that birds at noisy urban sites began singing earlier in the morning than birds at quiet sites. When temporary sound barriers reduced the noise, the urban birds gradually returned to later singing times. The findings suggest that ______

questions.explanation: D is correct because the birds changed their timing when noise conditions changed, indicating a flexible environmental response.
